# [TASK] Rename REACT_APP_ env vars to VITE_ and update all usages

## Task
CRA uses `REACT_APP_` prefix; Vite uses `VITE_`. Rename all env vars in `.env`, `.env.example`, `.env.production`, and all `process.env.REACT_APP_*` references in `src/` to `import.meta.env.VITE_*`.

## Parent Story
Parent: #122

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No `REACT_APP_` occurrences remain in any file under `frontend/filmpire/`.
- [x] All `process.env` references replaced with `import.meta.env`.
- [x] App loads API key from env var correctly in dev and production build.

## Estimate
**Hours:** 1

## Resolution
Renamed `REACT_APP_TMDB_KEY`, `REACT_APP_API_URL`, `REACT_APP_DISCOVERY_URL`,
`REACT_APP_KIBANA_URL`, `REACT_APP_GRAFANA_URL` to their `VITE_` equivalents
across `.env.example`, `TMDB.js`/`TMDB.test.js`, `media.js`/`media.test.js`,
`user.js`, `VoiceControl.jsx`, and `AdminDashboard.jsx`, swapping every
`process.env.X` read for `import.meta.env.X`. Also dropped the now-dead
CRA-only `ESLINT_NO_DEV_ERRORS=true` line from `.env.example` (no Vite
equivalent). `.env.production`'s `DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN=true` was left as-is —
not `REACT_APP_`-prefixed and out of this task's scope; worth a look under
#131 (npm audit/CI cleanup) if it's confirmed dead.

Verified: `grep -rn "REACT_APP_\|process\.env"` under `frontend/filmpire/`
returns nothing; `npm run build` (with `VITE_TMDB_KEY` set) succeeds and the
key is correctly inlined into the `dist/` bundle; `npm run dev` starts
cleanly; `npm run lint` is clean.

Note: `npm test` (`react-scripts test`) is already non-functional — confirmed
pre-existing from #125 (`react-scripts: not found`, unrelated to this
change), and explicitly deferred to #127 (Jest → Vitest). As an out-of-band
sanity check (not part of this task, not committed), I ran `TMDB.test.js`
and `media.test.js` under an ad hoc Vitest invocation: `import.meta.env`
parses and resolves correctly, and with `jest.fn` swapped for `vi.fn` (the
one thing #127 will fix) all 10 `TMDB.test.js` assertions pass — confirming
this rename is functionally correct for the eventual Vitest migration.
